summary: A 1934 30-foot pole L-4 tower in the Flathead National Forest; its page says Hungry Horse Reservoir submerged the site, a date that conflicts with the dam history.

facts.status_note: The lookout page says Hungry Horse Reservoir submerged the site.

events.note: 30-foot pole L-4 tower, per the lookout page.
Page says the site was submerged by the reservoir and gone in 1950. The Park Service dates dam completion to 1953, so the dates conflict.

evidence.supports: Built 1934 as a 30-foot pole L-4 tower
Site submerged by Hungry Horse Reservoir; gone 1950
evidence.quote: Site was submerged under water by the raising of Hungry Horse Reservoir. Gone 1950.

evidence.supports: About 12 miles southeast of Hungry Horse

evidence.quote: In 1953, Hungry Horse Dam was completed on the South Fork of the Flathead River

evidence.supports: Reservoir flooded one fire lookout tower, which was rebuilt elsewhere; tower not named
evidence.quote: When Hungry Horse Reservoir inundated a fire lookout tower, the Bureau of Reclamation rebuilt it elsewhere

notes_for_editor: The lookout page and the FFLA list agree on tower, gone and Flathead County. The date conflict is unresolved: the page gives gone in 1950 with the reservoir as cause, while the NPS gives 1953 for dam completion. The NPS article says a reservoir flooded a lookout tower that was rebuilt elsewhere, but it does not name the tower, so it is not linked to Riverside here. Leads not used: a Riverside Camp reminiscence (1915, a camp not a lookout, seen only in a search snippet) and Firefighter Mountain (Flathead NF, rebuilt 1953, no reservoir link in its own page). Elevation 3,550 ft is about 1,082 m. The record coordinates match the FFLA row. No corrections proposed.
